key_insight: Variational circuits can look statistically random long before they become hard to train, so complexity and trainability are not the same thing.
engineering_relevance: For quantum algorithm design, this means deeper or more expressive ansätze may still optimize well if they preserve locality and avoid full concentration-of-measure behavior.
method: Study structured variational circuits on the 1D cluster-Ising model and a generalized toric code Hamiltonian.
Track complexity with Porter-Thomas statistics, entanglement-spectrum level statistics, and inverse participation ratios.
Compare these diagnostics against variational optimization performance across increasing circuit depth.
evidence_signal: As depth increases, the measured complexity diagnostics move toward random-state or random-matrix-like behavior, yet optimization remains effective with no observed exponential gradient suppression in the studied regime.
watch_item: The result is limited to finite-depth structured circuits and the specific models studied, so it does not rule out barren plateaus in more global or highly random ansätze.
paper_title: Separation of Statistical Complexity and Trainability in Variational Quantum Circuits
